claim: The Widom 601 nucleosome positioning sequence can produce hexasomes in a specific orientation on DNA.
source: Here we show that the Widom 601 nucleosome positioning sequence can produce hexasomes in a specific orientation on DNA, providing a useful tool for interrogating chromatin enzymes and allowing for the generation of nucleosomes with precisely defined asymmetry.
evidence: Demonstrated through ExoIII digestion, histone mapping, and native PAGE experiments showing sequence-specific H2A/H2B dimer placement.

claim: The Chd1 chromatin remodeler from Saccharomyces cerevisiae requires H2A/H2B on the entry side for sliding.
source: Using this methodology, we demonstrate that the Chd1 chromatin remodeler from Saccharomyces cerevisiae requires H2A/H2B on the entry side for sliding, and thus, unlike the back-and-forth sliding observed for nucleosomes, Chd1 shifts hexasomes unidirectionally.
evidence: Demonstrated through histone mapping and stopped-flow fluorescence experiments comparing hexasomes with and without entry-side H2A/H2B.

claim: Chd1 shifts hexasomes unidirectionally, unlike the back-and-forth sliding observed for nucleosomes.
source: Using this methodology, we demonstrate that the Chd1 chromatin remodeler from Saccharomyces cerevisiae requires H2A/H2B on the entry side for sliding, and thus, unlike the back-and-forth sliding observed for nucleosomes, Chd1 shifts hexasomes unidirectionally.
evidence: Shown through histone mapping experiments demonstrating directional bias in hexasome sliding.

claim: Ubiquitin-conjugated H2B on the entry side stimulates nucleosome sliding by Chd1.
source: Chd1 takes part in chromatin reorganization surrounding transcribing RNA polymerase II (Pol II), and using asymmetric nucleosomes we show that ubiquitin-conjugated H2B on the entry side stimulates nucleosome sliding by Chd1.
evidence: Demonstrated through stopped-flow fluorescence experiments comparing nucleosomes with H2B-Ub on entry vs exit side.

claim: Hexasomes but not nucleosomes migrate differently by native PAGE when flanking DNA is on the left or right of the 601 sequence.
source: (A) Hexasomes but not nucleosomes migrate differently by native PAGE when flanking DNA is on the left or right of the 601 sequence.
evidence: Shown in Figure 1A comparing 0-601-80 and 80-601-0 preparations.

claim: The hexasome species lack one H2A/H2B dimer as shown by SDS-PAGE.
source: (D) As shown by SDS-PAGE, the hexasome species lack one H2A/H2B dimer.
evidence: Quantification shows H2A/H2B intensity in hexasomes was 47 ± 6% of that of nucleosomes.

claim: The preferred location of the remaining H2A/H2B dimer in the hexasome is determined in a sequence-specific fashion based on the orientation of the Widom 601.
source: Thus, the preferred location of the remaining H2A/H2B dimer in the hexasome was not influenced by flanking DNA, but instead was determined in a sequence-specific fashion based on the orientation of the Widom 601.
evidence: Demonstrated through ExoIII digestion experiments on 0-601-80 and 80-601-0 hexasomes.

claim: The side of the hexasome lacking the H2A/H2B dimer corresponds with the TA-poor side of the Widom 601 sequence.
source: With limiting amounts of H2A/H2B dimer, the side of the hexasome lacking the dimer (red dotted outline) corresponds with the TA-poor side of the Widom 601 sequence.
evidence: Shown through ExoIII digestion and histone mapping experiments.

claim: Addition of H2A/H2B dimer to hexasomes yields a protection pattern indistinguishable from nucleosomes in ExoIII digestion.
source: As shown in Figure 2B, addition of H2A/H2B dimer yielded a protection pattern indistinguishable from nucleosomes (lanes 22–24).
evidence: Demonstrated through ExoIII digestion experiments.

claim: Addition of H2A/H2B dimer to hexasomes is sufficient for recovering nucleosome-like protection patterns even in the absence of histone chaperones or elevated salt.
source: Therefore, even in the absence of histone chaperones or elevated salt, addition of H2A/H2B dimer to hexasomes was sufficient for recovering nucleosome-like protection patterns.
evidence: Shown through ExoIII digestion experiments.

claim: H2B cross-linking for hexasomes is virtually absent on the TA-poor side of the 601.
source: In agreement with ExoIII experiments, H2B cross-linking for hexasomes was virtually absent on the TA-poor side of the 601, whereas cross-linking on the TA-rich side was equivalent for hexasomes and nucleosomes (Figure 3; compare lane 1 with 2 and 4 with 5).
evidence: Demonstrated through histone mapping experiments using H2B-S53C labeled with APB.

claim: Addition of H2A/H2B fully recovered the H2B cross-link on the TA-poor side.
source: Strikingly, addition of H2A/H2B fully recovered the H2B cross-link on the TA-poor side (compare lanes 5 and 6), demonstrating that dimer addition generates correctly organized nucleosomes that are indistinguishable from those obtained by salt dialysis reconstitution.
evidence: Shown through histone mapping experiments.

claim: The 0-601-80 hexasomes, which lacked the entry-side H2A/H2B dimer, failed to show robust repositioning by Chd1.
source: For hexasomes, however, the ability of Chd1 to reposition was strongly dependent on the location of the single H2A/H2B dimer. The 0-601-80 hexasomes, which lacked the entry-side H2A/H2B dimer, failed to show robust repositioning, with the majority of products remaining at the starting position (lanes 4–6).
evidence: Demonstrated through histone mapping experiments.

claim: The 80-601-0 hexasomes shifted robustly onto flanking DNA, demonstrating that Chd1 activity can be supported by an H2A/H2B dimer on only the entry side.
source: In marked contrast, the 80-601-0 hexasomes shifted robustly onto flanking DNA, demonstrating that Chd1 activity can be supported by an H2A/H2B dimer on only the entry side (lanes 19–30).
evidence: Shown through histone mapping experiments.

claim: Chd1 shifted 80-601-0 hexasomes to the opposite end of DNA, farther than observed for nucleosomes.
source: Interestingly, instead of generating more centrally positioned products, Chd1 shifted 80-601-0 hexasomes to the opposite end of DNA, farther than observed for nucleosomes (Figure 4B).
evidence: Demonstrated through histone mapping experiments.

claim: The biased movement of 80-601-0 toward the entry H2A/H2B dimer indicates that it was the absence of H2A/H2B rather than the DNA sequence that blocked efficient sliding of 0-601-80 hexasomes.
source: This biased movement of 80-601-0 toward the entry H2A/H2B dimer, even after the hexasome had shifted away from its starting position on the 601 sequence, was consistent with much poorer sliding toward the side lacking the H2A/H2B dimer and indicated that it was the absence of H2A/H2B rather than the DNA sequence that blocked efficient sliding of 0-601-80 hexasomes.
evidence: Inferred from histone mapping experiments showing directional bias.

claim: Chd1 can reposition hexasomes, but the requirement for entry-side H2A/H2B yields a strong directional bias for hexasomes that contrasts with the back-and-forth sliding observed for nucleosomes.
source: Thus, Chd1 can reposition hexasomes, but the requirement for entry-side H2A/H2B yields a strong directional bias for hexasomes that contrasts with the back-and-forth sliding observed for nucleosomes.
evidence: Demonstrated through histone mapping experiments comparing nucleosome and hexasome sliding.

claim: Oriented hexasomes yielded a single, high-FRET population as expected for the H2A/H2B dimer located on the exit side, proximal to the DNA label.
source: In contrast, the oriented hexasomes yielded a single, high-FRET population as expected for the H2A/H2B dimer located on the exit side, proximal to the DNA label (Figure 5B).
evidence: Demonstrated through single-molecule FRET experiments.

claim: Addition of H2A/H2B dimer to hexasomes did not significantly alter the starting high-FRET population, yet incubation with Chd1 and ATP yielded a low-FRET profile similar to that observed for nucleosomes.
source: Addition of H2A/H2B dimer to hexasomes did not significantly alter the starting high-FRET population, yet incubation with Chd1 and ATP yielded a low-FRET profile similar to that observed for nucleosomes (Figure 5C).
evidence: Shown through single-molecule FRET experiments.

claim: The same cross-linking pattern was observed with 40-601-40 hexasomes as with nucleosomes, indicating that the ATP-bound state of the ATPase motor was not hindered by the lack of H2A/H2B on one side.
source: Strikingly, the same cross-linking pattern was also observed with 40-601-40 hexasomes (lanes 3, 6, 9 and 12), indicating that this ATP-bound state of the ATPase motor was not hindered by the lack of H2A/H2B on one side.
evidence: Demonstrated through Chd1 cross-linking experiments using N459C and V721C variants.

claim: The deficiency in sliding hexasomes lacking entry side H2A/H2B was likely a catalytic rather than a binding defect.
source: These results suggest that the deficiency in sliding hexasomes lacking entry side H2A/H2B was likely a catalytic rather than a binding defect.
evidence: Inferred from cross-linking experiments showing similar binding but different sliding activity.

claim: Chd1 shifted the hexasome much more rapidly when excess H2A/H2B was added to generate nucleosomes, with hexasome plus H2A/H2B dimer yielding a dominant, >300 fold faster rate of 0.57 s−1 compared to 0.0017 s−1 for hexasome alone.
source: Under these conditions, Chd1 shifted the hexasome much more rapidly when excess H2A/H2B was added to generate nucleosomes (Figure 6B). Both reactions were fit to double exponentials, with hexasome alone dominated by a slower rate of 0.0017 s−1, whereas hexasome plus H2A/H2B dimer yielded a dominant, >300 fold faster rate of 0.57 s−1.
evidence: Demonstrated through stopped-flow SQOF experiments.

claim: The ability of Chd1 to shift hexasomes lacking the entry side H2A/H2B dimer is extremely poor.
source: Taken together, these experiments demonstrate that the ability of Chd1 to shift hexasomes lacking the entry side H2A/H2B dimer is extremely poor.
evidence: Demonstrated through stopped-flow experiments and histone mapping.

claim: Adding H2A/H2B to hexasomes produces nucleosomes that are similar to and apparently more homogeneous than those produced by salt dialysis.
source: These results suggest that adding H2A/H2B to hexasomes produces nucleosomes that are similar to and apparently more homogeneous than those produced by salt dialysis.
evidence: Inferred from stopped-flow experiments comparing hexasome plus dimer to salt-dialyzed nucleosomes.

claim: Nucleosome sliding rates with the H2B Y39A/M56A variant were indistinguishable from wild type, indicating that Chd1 does not require these residues on the entry side dimer for normal activity.
source: Nucleosome sliding rates with this H2B variant (Figure 7, cyan) were indistinguishable from wild type, indicating that Chd1 does not require these residues on the entry side dimer for normal activity.
evidence: Demonstrated through stopped-flow experiments with H2B-Y39A/M56A variant.

claim: Chd1 mobilized nucleosomes containing truncated H2A lacking residues 110–129 on the entry dimer 2.5-fold faster than wild type.
source: Interestingly, Chd1 mobilized nucleosomes containing this truncated H2A on the entry dimer 2.5-fold faster than wild type (Figure 7, green).
evidence: Demonstrated through stopped-flow experiments with H2A Δ110-129 variant.

claim: The H2A C-terminus does not contain a critical epitope for Chd1.
source: Thus, the H2A C-terminus does not contain a critical epitope for Chd1, and faster sliding may have been achieved by altered histone-histone or histone-DNA dynamics.
evidence: Inferred from faster sliding rates with H2A C-terminal truncation.

claim: Each of the H2A acidic patch mutations resulted in a two-fold decrease in Chd1 nucleosome sliding rates.
source: In comparison to wild type H2A, each of these H2A mutations resulted in a two-fold decrease in Chd1 nucleosome sliding rates (Figure 7, brown, orange, and magenta).
evidence: Demonstrated through stopped-flow experiments with H2A acidic patch variants.

claim: The H2A acidic patch is not a critical epitope required for Chd1 sliding.
source: These modest rate decreases suggest that the H2A acidic patch is not a critical epitope required for Chd1 sliding.
evidence: Inferred from modest rate decreases with acidic patch mutations.

claim: The reduced rate with acidic patch mutations suggests a catalytic rather than a binding defect.
source: However, it is interesting to note that these reactions were performed with saturating Chd1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 2), and therefore the reduced rate, while modest, suggests a catalytic rather than a binding defect.
evidence: Inferred from experiments performed at saturating Chd1 concentrations.

claim: The two nucleosomes containing entry-side H2B-Ub (Wt-Ub and Ub-Ub) yielded faster rates than nucleosomes with unmodified entry-side H2B.
source: In fact, the two nucleosomes containing entry-side H2B-Ub (Wt-Ub and Ub-Ub) yielded faster rates than nucleosomes with unmodified entry-side H2B (Figure 8B).
evidence: Demonstrated through Cy3-Cy3 SQOF experiments.

claim: Nucleosomes containing entry-side H2B-Ub consistently showed faster rates of sliding.
source: In agreement with a preferential stimulation of Chd1, nucleosomes containing entry-side H2B-Ub consistently showed faster rates of sliding (Figure 8C,D).
evidence: Demonstrated through stopped-flow experiments with Cy3B-Dabcyl.

claim: H2B-Ub did not merely improve Chd1 binding but increased catalytic turnover.
source: These experiments were conducted with saturating Chd1 (400 nM) indicating that H2B-Ub did not merely improve Chd1 binding but increased catalytic turnover.
evidence: Inferred from experiments performed at saturating Chd1 concentrations.

claim: One side of the 601 has a much higher affinity for H2A/H2B than the other, resulting in preferential salt-deposition of the dimer in a sequence-specific fashion.
source: We generated hexasomes from nucleosome reconstitutions in the presence of limiting H2A/H2B dimer, and our work indicates that one side of the 601 has a much higher affinity for H2A/H2B than the other, resulting in preferential salt-deposition of the dimer in a sequence-specific fashion (Figure 2).
evidence: Demonstrated through ExoIII and histone mapping experiments.

claim: The biased orientation of hexasomes may arise from the asymmetric distribution of inward-facing minor groove TA steps flanking the nucleosome dyad.
source: While identification of sequence elements responsible for preferred H2A/H2B deposition requires further investigations, we speculate that the biased orientation of hexasomes may arise from the asymmetric distribution of inward-facing minor groove TA steps flanking the nucleosome dyad.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on known properties of the Widom 601 sequence.

claim: The Widom 601 is well known for its marked asymmetry in strength of histone-DNA contacts.
source: The Widom 601 is well known for its marked asymmetry in strength of histone-DNA contacts (Hall et al., 2009), and higher salt resistance of the TA-rich side of the 601 (Chua et al., 2012) is consistent with the preferential H2A/H2B deposition that yields oriented hexasomes.
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The entry-side dimer is critical for robust sliding by Chd1.
source: We show that the entry-side dimer is critical for robust sliding by Chd1, which results in a strongly biased repositioning of hexasomes toward the side with the H2A/H2B dimer (Figure 4).
evidence: Demonstrated through histone mapping and stopped-flow experiments.

claim: The absence of one H2A/H2B dimer does not appear to diminish binding of the Chd1 ATPase motor to either SHL2 site of the hexasome.
source: As shown by cross-linking, the absence of one H2A/H2B dimer does not appear to diminish binding of the Chd1 ATPase motor to either SHL2 site of the hexasome (Figure 6A), strongly suggesting that the defect in sliding occurs after engagement of the remodeler.
evidence: Demonstrated through cross-linking experiments.

claim: Rather than a specific interaction with the entry side H2A/H2B dimer, Chd1 may instead be responding to DNA unwrapping.
source: One explanation for our findings is that rather than a specific interaction with the entry side H2A/H2B dimer, Chd1 may instead be responding to DNA unwrapping.
evidence: Speculative explanation based on experimental findings.

claim: Sensitivity to DNA unwrapping is consistent with slower nucleosome sliding activity of Chd1 when a transcription factor is bound on the entry side of the nucleosome.
source: Sensitivity to DNA unwrapping is consistent with slower nucleosome sliding activity of Chd1 when a transcription factor is bound on the entry side of the nucleosome (Nodelman et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The directional sliding of hexasomes by Chd1 likely influences chromatin organization in vivo.
source: The directional sliding of hexasomes by Chd1, which contrasts with the back-and-forth movement typical for nucleosomes, likely influences chromatin organization in vivo.
evidence: Speculative inference based on experimental findings.

claim: Both transcription through nucleosomes by Pol II and remodeling by RSC along with the NAP1 chaperone have been shown to generate hexasomes.
source: In vitro, both transcription through nucleosomes by Pol II and remodeling by RSC along with the NAP1 chaperone have been shown to generate hexasomes (Kireeva et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The passage of Pol II has been shown to specifically displace the H2A/H2B dimer distal to the promoter.
source: Although histone chaperones such as FACT would be expected to replace the missing H2A/H2B dimer during transcription, the passage of Pol II has been shown to specifically displace the H2A/H2B dimer distal to the promoter (Hsieh et al., 2013; Kulaeva et al., 2009), which would orient hexasomes for biased sliding toward the 5' end.
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Nucleosome array packing against the +1 nucleosome is dependent on Chd1 and ISWI chromatin remodelers.
source: One speculative idea is that nucleosome array packing against the +1 nucleosome, which is dependent on Chd1 and ISWI chromatin remodelers (Gkikopoulos et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2011), would be favored by directional hexasome sliding (Figure 9).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Inactivation of Pol II relaxes nucleosome packing in coding regions, resulting in a nucleosome drift of ~10 bp toward the 3' end of yeast genes.
source: Consistent with this idea, it has been shown that inactivation of Pol II relaxes nucleosome packing in coding regions, resulting in a nucleosome drift of ~10 bp toward the 3' end of yeast genes (Weiner et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Oriented hexasomes are a useful tool for generating specifically oriented asymmetric nucleosomes.
source: Our work also demonstrates how hexasomes made using the Widom 601 are a useful tool for generating specifically oriented asymmetric nucleosomes.
evidence: Demonstrated through smFRET and H2B-Ub experiments.

claim: Single molecule FRET experiments require a single, specifically positioned donor-acceptor pair to extract meaningful information on nucleosome dynamics.
source: To extract meaningful information on nucleosome dynamics, single molecule FRET experiments require a single, specifically positioned donor-acceptor pair (Blosser et al., 2009; Deindl et al., 2013; Ngo et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Due to the pseudo two-fold symmetry of the nucleosome, labeling any of the histones with a FRET fluorophore typically yields three different labeling configurations.
source: However, due to the pseudo two-fold symmetry of the nucleosome, labeling any of the histones with a FRET fluorophore (donor or acceptor) typically yields three different labeling configurations (Deindl et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Oriented hexasomes can yield a homogeneously labeled population that greatly facilitates smFRET experiments.
source: Here, we show how oriented hexasomes can yield a homogeneously labeled population (Figure 5) that greatly facilitates smFRET experiments.
evidence: Demonstrated through smFRET experiments.

claim: The stimulatory effect of ubiquitin was observed even with saturating remodeler concentrations, indicating that it is not merely the result of improved Chd1 binding.
source: Unexpectedly, the stimulatory effect of ubiquitin was observed even with saturating remodeler concentrations, indicating that it is not merely the result of improved Chd1 binding.
evidence: Demonstrated through stopped-flow experiments at saturating Chd1.

claim: H2B-Ub is required for maximum stimulation of Pol II transcription by FACT, potentially through aiding displacement of H2A/H2B.
source: Interestingly, H2B-Ub is required for maximum stimulation of Pol II transcription by FACT, potentially through aiding displacement of H2A/H2B (Pavri et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Nucleosomes are often asymmetric in biological contexts, functionalized with post-translational modifications (PTMs), substituted with histone variants, and even lacking H2A/H2B dimers.
source: Despite their canonical two-fold symmetry, nucleosomes in biological contexts are often asymmetric: functionalized with post-translational modifications (PTMs), substituted with histone variants, and even lacking H2A/H2B dimers.
evidence: General statement supported by context and citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Asymmetry occurs when each copy of a histone possesses distinct epigenetic modifications.
source: Since the nucleosome is pseudo-symmetric with two copies of each core histone (H2A, H2B, H3 and H4), asymmetry occurs when each copy possesses distinct epigenetic modifications.
evidence: Definitional statement based on nucleosome structure.

claim: Recent advances have revealed asymmetry at the single nucleosome level.
source: Recent advances have revealed asymmetry at the single nucleosome level (Rhee et al., 2014; Voigt et al., 2012), yet with challenges in synthesizing uniform populations of asymmetrically modified nucleosomes (Lechner et al., 2016; Liokatis et al., 2016), the biological significance of the vast majority of asymmetric marks remains unclear.
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Trimethylation of H3K27 is carried out by PRC2.
source: Trimethylation of H3K27 is carried out by PRC2, and while H3K4me3 blocks modification of K27 on the same H3 tail, PRC2 can deposit a H3K27me3 mark on the opposing H3 tail of the same nucleosome (Lechner et al., 2016; Voigt et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: PRC2 is activated by the mark it deposits, with substrate preference for asymmetric nucleosomes containing one H3K27me3.
source: In addition to generating nucleosomes with asymmetric H3K4me3/H3K27me3, PRC2 is also activated by the mark it deposits, with substrate preference for asymmetric nucleosomes containing one H3K27me3 (Lechner et al., 2016; Margueron et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Genome-wide studies have revealed that the +1 nucleosome is strikingly asymmetric with regards to H3K9 acetylation, H2B ubiquitination, and residency of H2A.Z.
source: Genome-wide studies have revealed that the +1 nucleosome is strikingly asymmetric with regards to H3K9 acetylation, H2B ubiquitination, and residency of H2A.Z (Rhee et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Asymmetric marks of the +1 nucleosome correlate with asymmetric localization of the RSC, INO80, and SWR1 chromatin remodelers.
source: Asymmetric marks of the +1 nucleosome correlate with asymmetric localization of the RSC, INO80, and SWR1 chromatin remodelers (Ramachandran et al., 2015; Yen et al., 2012), and a major question is how these and other enzymes generate and read-out the asymmetric distribution of these marks.
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The existence of hexasomes in vivo has been supported by ChIP-exo and MNase-seq experiments.
source: The existence of hexasomes in vivo has been supported by ChIP-exo and MNase-seq experiments (Rhee et al., 2014), and in vitro, hexasomes have been shown to be generated by the RSC remodeler with the NAP1 histone chaperone (Kuryan et al., 2012) and also by RNA polymerase II (Pol II) transcribing through nucleosomes (Kireeva et al., 2002, 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Pol II successfully transcribes through hexasomes oriented with the promoter-distal H2A/H2B dimer missing, but stalls in the absence of the promoter-proximal dimer.
source: Intriguingly, Pol II successfully transcribes through hexasomes oriented with the promoter-distal H2A/H2B dimer missing, but stalls in the absence of the promoter-proximal dimer (Kulaeva et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Chd1 and ISWI reposition nucleosomes into evenly spaced arrays, and are required for packing arrays of nucleosomes against the +1 nucleosome.
source: Chd1 and ISWI reposition nucleosomes into evenly spaced arrays, and are required for packing arrays of nucleosomes against the +1 nucleosome (Gkikopoulos et al., 2011; Lusser et al., 2005; Pointner et al., 2012; Tsukiyama et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Specific binding of H3K4me3 by the chromodomains of mouse Chd1 has been correlated with its localization to the promoter.
source: Although specific binding of H3K4me3 by the chromodomains of mouse Chd1 has been correlated with its localization to the promoter (Lin et al., 2011), Chd1 and ISWI remodelers have been shown to participate in resetting the chromatin barrier in coding regions after passage of Pol II, required for preventing cryptic transcription (Cheung et al., 2008; Pointner et al., 2012; Radman-Livaja et al., 2012; Smolle et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Chd1 has been linked to elongating Pol II through interactions with the transcriptional elongation factors FACT and Spt4-Spt5, and with the Rtf1 subunit of the PAF complex.
source: Chd1 has been linked to elongating Pol II through interactions with the transcriptional elongation factors FACT and Spt4-Spt5, and with the Rtf1 subunit of the PAF complex (Kelley et al., 1999; Krogan et al., 2002; Simic et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Passage of Pol II is coupled to transient ubiquitination of H2B.
source: In addition to potentially generating hexasomes, passage of Pol II is also coupled to transient ubiquitination of H2B (Fleming et al., 2008; Xiao et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The H2B-Ubiquitin (H2B-Ub) mark is required for FACT-assisted disruption of the chromatin barrier.
source: Interestingly, the H2B-Ubiquitin (H2B-Ub) mark is required for FACT-assisted disruption of the chromatin barrier (Pavri et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Chd1 has been shown to be required for high levels of transcription-coupled ubiquitination of H2B in vivo.
source: Chd1 has been shown to be required for high levels of transcription-coupled ubiquitination of H2B in vivo (Lee et al., 2012), yet a direct connection between Chd1 and transcriptionally altered nucleosomes has remained elusive.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work.
